text:
ana: quick question from the pricing Q&A — when we hand out promo credits to pilots, do those ever automatically expand their quota or just reduce invoices?

matt: important distinction: promo credits reduce the billing balance by default. they do not change token/embedding quotas automatically. there is a separate "promo->quota" manual action we can take for strategic pilots.

rosie: is there any plan to make that mapping self-serve for growth customers? ops is overloaded.

matt: exploring a controlled self-serve flow: a one-click "apply credits to quota" in the billing console limited to certain plans and with audit logging. would require controls to avoid accidental overspend.

ana: sorry small nit — can we surface the effective burn rate (tokens/credit) in the UI so customers know how far promo credits go?

robie: absolutely. we'll show a breakdown: credits -> token-equivalent by model family, plus an estimated days-left given current usage.

ana: another ask: webhooks for quota events — CS wants to trigger workflows when a pilot hits 80%/95%.

matt: good idea. we can add an org-level webhook: POST /webhooks/org_usage with events: quota_threshold_reached, quota_exceeded, credit_balance_low. payload will include org_id, quota_type, percent_used, and an admin_url.

rosie: what about short-lived spikes? some customers get transient bursts during load tests. do we immediately block them?

matt: we have a soft-cap + burst policy. default soft-cap warns and returns 200 with header X-Quota-Status: soft_limit_exceeded; requests continue for a configurable grace window (default 600s). after grace expires, we return 429 with an error body. ops can configure grace duration per org.

finance-bot: system: note created: invoice-impact-check #5590 for promo->quota flow.

ana: error payloads — can we make quota errors actionable in SDKs? mobile team wants a field to show UI prompts.

matt: proposal: quota exceeded -> 429 with JSON: {"error":"quota_exceeded","quota_type":"tokens|embeddings","grace_remaining":int (secs, 0 if none),"admin_url":"https://console"}. rate limit -> 429 with {"error":"rate_limited","retry_after":int}. SDKs can use grace_remaining to surface an "apply for temporary top-up" CTA.

rosie: product ask: can we return an opt-in header that shows remaining tokens for the key owner? earlier threads suggested X-Remaining-Quota — is webhook + header overkill?

matt: we'll do both but opt-in. header X-Redwood-Quota: tokens=12345;embeddings=80 (only when the key owner enables it) and org_usage webhooks for async alerts. both need admin scope.

ana: last one: dedicated customers — do they get these webhooks and grace policies too?

matt: yes, dedicated can enable the same control plane features. for Dedicated we typically map quotas to committed capacity, so grace windows are shorter and handled by SRE playbooks.

all-hands-bot: follow-ups created: #5590 invoice-impact-check, #5591 webhook-org-usage, #5592 billing-credits-ui

ana: thanks, that's super helpful. will forward to CS and mobile.
